subject: Scaling acceleration — proposed uplift amortization & co-term options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.health>, procurement@acme.health
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scaling acceleration — proposed uplift amortization & co-term options

Hi Sara / Acme procurement team,

Following our renewal conversation last week, we ran a few scenarios for the mid-contract top-up you mentioned (approx. 2.3x current committed units). To make procurement and budget timing easier, attached are two pragmatic paths:

- Option A: Immediate uplift billed pro-rata, standard 30-day invoice (one-time charge).
- Option B: Uplift amortized over the remaining contract term (co-term to Oct 31, 2028) with quarterly invoicing and a 7% amortization fee to cover committed capacity scheduling.
- Option C: Staged ramp — 60% now (pro-rata), 40% after Q3 with a reduced amortization fee (4%).

Key notes: all options preserve the renewal discount band we previously discussed (15% base discount on committed units), but Option B smooths cashflow and keeps your effective unit cost lower month-to-month. I attached a short workbook that shows monthly run rates and invoice examples.

Ask: can you share which payment cadence Procurement prefers (one-time vs quarterly amortized)? If Option B looks viable we can draft a one-line amendment and a short SOW for services ramp. Priyom / Kimberly — looping you in for legal/invoice terms and to confirm we can accommodate the co-term to Oct 31, 2028.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0193

Attachments: Uplift_Options_v3.xlsx, SOW_draft_Acme_2027.pdf

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.health
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling acceleration — proposed uplift amortization & co-term options

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs before Procurement will run it up the chain: 

1) For Option B, does the 7% amortization fee apply to the total uplift dollars or only to the portion we amortize?
2) If we co-term to Oct 31, 2028, will that change our renewal anchor pricing for next cycle? We want to avoid an accidental step-up.
3) Is the SOW a hard dependency for the uplift or can we amend capacity only and add SOW later?

Timeline: Procurement needs final invoice terms by end of next Tuesday (4/20) to make the May payment window. We prefer quarterly invoicing if there is no large upfront hit.

—Sara
Sara Patel | Head of Machine Learning Platforms
Acme Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 12:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling acceleration — proposed uplift amortization & co-term options

Sara — quick answers inline and a short ask.

1) Amortization fee: the 7% applies only to the amortized portion. So if you amortize $100k of the uplift and pay the rest up front, the fee is charged against that $100k only.

2) Co-term and renewal anchor: we will explicitly pin the renewal anchor to the pre-uplift baseline in the amendment language (so the uplift does not inflate your future anchor). The legal team has signoff on that approach in principle — Kimberly, confirm below?

3) SOW dependency: the SOW is optional for capacity-only changes — we include a short SOW if you want prioritized onboarding/optimize support. The uplift amendment can stand alone for billing + service-level notes.

Suggested next step: If Procurement is okay with quarterly invoicing and amortization, I can send a redlineable one-page amendment + optional SOW for signatures by EOW. Priyom / Kimberly — can you confirm we can ship the amendment template and the anchor language ASAP?

Thanks,
Ben

> On Thu, Apr 15, 2027 at 10:03 AM Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.health> wrote:
> > (reply)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:47:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling acceleration — proposed uplift amortization & co-term options

Ben / Priyom — confirmed: we can (a) produce a one-page amendment that (i) adds the uplift units, (ii) defines amortization on the specified portion and (iii) explicitly states the renewal anchor remains based on the original committed baseline. Legal will include language like: 

"The Parties agree that increased committed units and any associated amortization fees reflected in this Amendment shall not increase Customer's baseline for future renewal discount bands; baseline for renewal calculations shall remain the committed units in effect immediately prior to this Amendment."

A couple operational notes: 
- We prefer to avoid multi-year co-term resets that change billing cadence mid-invoice cycle; let's set co-term date to the last day of the month (Oct 31) and start quarterly invoicing aligned to Q-end.
- We need Procurement's PO number on the amendment before signature.

I will draft the amendment and attach to the SOW. Priyom — can you verify the price calc in Ben's workbook matches our billing system export? If not, flag discrepancies.

kim
Kimberly Park | Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acme.health>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme.health
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scaling acceleration — proposed uplift amortization & co-term options

Ben / Kimberly / Priyom — thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement confirms we will move forward with Option B (amortized uplift) subject to: 

- Quarterly invoicing, amortization fee applied only to amortized portion.
- Co-term set to Oct 31, 2028 with renewal anchor explicitly preserved as you described.
- We will provide the PO number by 4/21 and sign the one-page amendment + SOW for priority onboarding.

Please send the redlineable amendment and the SOW so we can circulate internally this week. Once we receive the PO, we can confirm the May payment window.

—Sara
Sara Patel | Head of Machine Learning Platforms
Acme Health

Attachments referenced: SOW_draft_Acme_2027.pdf, Uplift_Options_v3.xlsx
thread_summary: Customer (Acme Health) chooses amortized uplift (Option B). Redwood legal will draft a one-page amendment preserving renewal anchor; procurement to provide PO by 2027-04-21. Quarterly invoicing and co-term to 2028-10-31 agreed in principle.
